doc.title: Vince Lateano interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 8, 2002

title: Cal Tjader's death in Manila
summary: Cal died of cardiac arrest in the Philippines in May 1982, four years after Lateano joined.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: And Cal unfortunately, you were with him, playing with him when he passed away.

Exactly. Almost four years to the day almost. He passed away in the Philippines in Manila on Cinco de Mayo, the fifth of May, in 1982. So I joined May ’78, so four years. And that was a sad, tragic situation. We went — he was in the service during World War II. He was in the Navy and I think he was a Corpsman, a medical Corpsman. And he was in the Philippines towards the end of the war, and he sort of had an affinity for the place. In fact if you do any research, on his compositions he wrote tunes, “Mindanao,” he wrote three or four tunes with Philippine island titles. So he’d been asked to go there a few times and sort of always put it off. And then his health wasn’t good, when he decided to go, because they’d been asking him to go. And his wife didn’t want him to go. But we went, and she went with him, and we got there, we didn’t play a note. We got there, it was a long flight, we got there on an early Monday morning and he was restless and Tuesday he wasn’t feeling good, and then Tuesday evening he went into a cardiac arrest and passed away the next day. So it was very, very unusual situation, to be that far away. And then we had to wait four or five days before we could all leave together, because we weren’t leaving otherwise, without Cal, because of the bureaucratic thing. And it took a while to come back from that. You know? Plus he was a great, he was a wonderful guy. Funny, a good guy to work for, and obviously a good musician.
